twentysecond.why-the-22nd.nohad-dreamed-: , Nohad dreamed that Saint Charbel, accompanied by another monk, performed surgery on her. He told her:
twentysecond.why-the-22nd.i-performed-th: "I performed the surgery to help people regain their faith. I ask you to visit my hermitage in Annaya on the 22nd of every month and attend Mass regularly for the rest of your life."
twentysecond.why-the-22nd.she-awoke-heal: She awoke healed, bearing two small scars on her neck - and she kept that monthly pilgrimage for the rest of her life, until her death in May 2025. The request in her testimony was addressed to her. The Church does not make it a rule for anyone else. Others healed through Saint Charbel's intercession have reported similar dreams of "surgery" in the night.

twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.is: Is the 22nd of the month an official feast of the Church?
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.no: No. The liturgical feasts are July 24 in the universal calendar and the third Sunday of July in the Maronite Church - see the
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.th: . The 22nd is a devotional custom that grew from Nohad El Shami's healing in 1993 and the monthly pilgrimage she kept afterward. It is loved and widely observed, but it is a tradition of the faithful, not a decree.
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.do: Do I have to be at Annaya to keep the 22nd?
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.no: No. Saint Charbel's reported words to Nohad asked her to visit the hermitage monthly - that was her call, and pilgrims who can go, go. But the day is kept just as fully at home: Mass, the Rosary, a candle, the holy oil, a prayer for your intention. Maronite parishes on every continent now hold 22nd-of-the-month Masses - see

twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.ca: Can I ask Saint Charbel for healing on the 22nd?
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.ye: Yes - that is what the day is for. The
twentysecond.common-questions-about-t.pa: page has words for a sick loved one and for yourself. One honest note, as always on this site: prayer asks, and God remains free - no date or formula guarantees an outcome. The holy oil, a pilgrimage and prayer do not take the place of medical care. If you are praying with someone who is ill, you can also stay with them and help in practical ways.
